questions.question: Name the four phases of a warm up in the correct order.

points.text: Pulse raiser, stretching, skill practice, mental preparation.

questions.question: Explain how a pulse raiser reduces the risk of injury during exercise.

points.text: The pulse raiser gradually increases heart rate and body temperature. Warmer muscles are more pliable and elastic, reducing the risk of tears and strains. Increased blood flow delivers more oxygen to muscles and synovial fluid is released to lubricate joints.

questions.question: Why is dynamic stretching preferred over static stretching in a warm up?

points.text: Dynamic stretching involves moving muscles through their range of motion, mimicking the movements of the upcoming activity. This actively prepares the neuromuscular system. Static stretching can actually reduce muscle power output and is better suited to cool downs.

questions.question: Describe the role of the cool down in removing lactic acid from the body.

points.text: The cool down maintains an elevated heart rate and continued blood flow. This circulating blood transports lactic acid from the muscles to the liver, where it is converted back to pyruvic acid and then either used for energy or converted to glycogen for storage.

questions.question: Explain what is meant by blood pooling and how a cool down prevents it.

points.text: Blood pooling occurs when exercise stops suddenly and blood collects in the lower extremities due to gravity, as the muscle pump is no longer active. This reduces blood return to the heart and brain, causing dizziness or fainting. A cool down maintains gentle muscular contraction, keeping the muscle pump active and blood returning to the heart.

questions.question: How does mental preparation as part of a warm up benefit a competitive performer?

points.text: Mental preparation helps the performer focus on the task, improves concentration, builds confidence through visualisation, and ensures the performer is psychologically ready to compete at their best. It can also help manage pre-competition anxiety.
